replacements.text: The acceptance-criteria standard asks whether each commitment has a criterion, and another rule asks whether each criterion names a check. The second rule opened with a sentence that asked whether a commitment had a criterion, so its reviewer filed coverage gaps under that rule. The second rule now judges the check each criterion names. On the corrected control document, 9 of 10 panel runs returned an empty report, up from 2 of 10. All 10 runs on the defective document still objected to the planted criterion.
The rule text is part of each emitted prompt. Every existing attack record's fingerprint changes as a result.
All 10 runs on the defective document still objected to the planted criterion under the planted rule.
Ten runs per document used the same model and effort. The one remaining control objection cites a flaw present in both versions of the document.

The `verification-contract` rule opened with a sentence that asked whether a commitment had a criterion. Its reviewer filed coverage gaps under that rule. The rule now judges each criterion's own check and sends the question of whether a commitment has a criterion to coverage.
The attack skill's table gains a column naming what each reviewer reads. That unit determines who owns each rule.
